summary.name: Sticker-Style Explainer Animation
summary.visualIdentity: Supplemental, user-requested guidance combining friendly sticker graphics with educational explanation, not a formal art movement. Scientific objects use rounded silhouettes, consistent white borders and light shadows; stable colors or symbols identify concepts. Short labels and purposeful arrows guide a question-to-mechanism-to-conclusion sequence.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit cues suit science and concept explainers. Inferred fits include classroom lessons, health or climate communication, and concise social explainers. It can stand alone or support charts and teacher-like annotations when those clarify the idea.
summary.limitations: Decoration must not obscure the explanation; keep labels short and relationships clear. Avoid bouncing chart marks, covered axes or values, cluttered notes, and transitions that hide causality. The suggested colors are not canonical: approved task or brand palettes take precedence. Contrast suggestions need checking on actual frames.
summary.palette: Suggested tokens for new artwork only: background #F5EFDF; foreground #2C424D; white #FFFFFF reserved for consistent sticker borders; teal #73A59E and warm #D28C67 as subordinate concept accents. Use discrete colors, no palette gradient. Teal and warm accents with foreground text miss the stated normal-text contrast target; use a contrasting existing backing and verify composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Place, peel, move along paths, and use restrained bounce to clarify concepts. Reveal objects and relationships in explanatory order; arrows should communicate purposeful relationships. In HTML, a stepper can update chart and sticker states, with accessible data and transcript. Video motion must derive from shared seekable time; interactive scroll or pointer input is not a video clock. Keep reverse and direct seeks coherent, and hide labels until their container is fully revealed.
summary.audio: No fixed genre, tempo, voice, or required audio layer is specified. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; leave speech and reading holds clear. Honor supplied assets and explicit choices. Select or create audio separately, then synchronize and mix it with picture.
summary.assetRequirements: No required uploads are specified. Build transparent stickers, SVG charts, and real text in a shared scene coordinate system; preserve approved source assets and exact colors. Pan or scale scene containers instead of relying on an oversized bitmap. Suggested palette values are optional; do not treat tool recommendations as proof of local availability.
summary.combinations: Suggested: style-097 charts for a few factual figures, keeping chart marks flat, accurate, and unbordered while stickers retain stable concept colors; or style-024 foreground-colored handwritten arrows and brief notes after sticker placement, with arrows reserved for causality. These are optional. Keep stickers clear of chart data and notes from competing with labels or peel motion.
summary.productionApproach: Choose SVG for scalable stickers, charts, masks, and strokes; use D3 when chart layout or scales help, and PixiJS only if many sprites warrant it. GSAP is a suggested motion owner; ensure all state is deterministic and seekable. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required output. Pipeline choice must not dictate the visual style.
